There is a particular kind of winter skin surprise: your usual moisturizer is still there, but by the afternoon your cheeks feel tight. Meanwhile, your forehead might be as shiny as ever. Sound familiar?

Cold air, indoor heating and long, hot showers can all leave skin feeling drier. A moisturizer helps reduce water loss, but a cream that feels comforting to one person can feel heavy to another. Rather than picking the most talked-about tube, start with what your skin needs—and how much cream you actually enjoy wearing.

01 / AESTURA

AESTURA Ato Barrier 365 Cream

The face-cream option

For skin that starts feeling tight in the cold, AESTURA is a useful place to begin if you like a cream rather than a watery gel. The YesStyle listing describes a moisturizer with a ceramide-related complex, cholesterol and fatty acids; the brand highlights its visible moisturizing capsules.1

Think of it as the dedicated face-cream choice in this edit. You can use it after cleansing and any optional serum, then follow with sunscreen in the morning. It is not necessary to add a separate toner or essence if your skin already feels comfortable.

03 / DR. ALTHEA

Dr. Althea 345 Relief Cream

The lighter-feeling option

Winter does not automatically turn every face into dry skin. If your T-zone still gets oily or you simply dislike a thick finish, 345 Relief Cream offers a different starting point. YesStyle describes it as a lightweight gel cream, while Dr. Althea presents it as a daily moisturizer for sensitive and acne-prone skin.3

Its current brand ingredient list includes glycerin, niacinamide, panthenol and tea tree leaf water. It is a moisturizer—not an acne treatment—and a “non-comedogenic” claim cannot guarantee that every person's skin will respond the same way.

Before you buy: A lighter feel can be appealing under makeup, but very dry skin may need something more cushioning. Consider a richer cream instead, or add a little plain petrolatum to particularly dry spots if it suits your skin. Check the formula if you are sensitive to tea tree or other listed ingredients.

02 — Find your fit

How to choose a moisturizer for winter

Start with how your skin feels

If your whole face feels tight or looks flaky, a more substantial cream may feel more comfortable than a thin gel. If only your cheeks are dry, try a little more moisturizer there rather than covering your entire face in a thick layer. Oilier areas still need moisture; they may simply prefer a lighter texture or a smaller amount.

Look at the whole formula, not just one ingredient

Glycerin and hyaluronic acid are humectants, which help attract water. Emollients help soften skin, while ingredients such as dimethicone or petrolatum can help reduce moisture loss. Ceramides are skin-identical lipids often included in barrier-supporting formulas. No single ingredient or marketing term tells you exactly how rich a finished product will feel.

Check the version and the size

A familiar name can have different regional formulas, renewed packaging or a similarly named lotion. Check that you are ordering the cream and the size you want. If you are sensitive to a particular ingredient, use the ingredient list on the product you receive rather than relying on a review of an older version.

Give your routine room to breathe

You do not need to buy all three. Apply the moisturizer you choose to slightly damp skin after cleansing; add optional treatments only if they suit you. In the morning, finish with a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher. The American Academy of Dermatology also recommends gentle cleansing and avoiding very hot, long showers when skin is dry.4

03 — Your questions

Frequently asked questions

Which is better for very dry winter skin: AESTURA or ILLIYOON?

Both are cream options designed around moisturizing and barrier support. AESTURA is a face-cream starting point; ILLIYOON's larger tube can also be used on the body. There is no reliable way to promise which will feel richer or work better on your skin without trying them. Choose by preferred size, ingredients and texture, then introduce the product cautiously.

Is Dr. Althea 345 enough for winter?

It might be if your skin stays comfortable with a lightweight gel cream. If tightness or flaky patches continue, try a more moisturizing cream rather than assuming you need another serum. In particularly dry spots, a small amount of petrolatum over moisturizer may help reduce water loss if tolerated.

Do I need a ceramide cream and a hydrating serum?

Not necessarily. A moisturizer can provide hydration and reduce water loss on its own. A hydrating serum is an optional extra if you enjoy it or find it useful; it is not a substitute for moisturizer when your skin needs a more protective layer.

What if my skin stings when I apply moisturizer?

Stop using a product that causes irritation. If your skin keeps burning or stinging, is cracked or persistently itchy, or does not improve with gentle care, speak with a dermatologist rather than treating a shopping guide as a diagnosis. Follow your clinician's advice for any prescribed treatments.

The takeaway

A comfortable routine beats a crowded shelf

Start with a texture you like, check the ingredients and size, and give your skin time to tell you whether it needs more. The best winter moisturizer is not necessarily the richest or most viral one—it is the one that fits your skin and your routine.
